field_changes.before: "Right to Compute Act." Creates a right to use computational resources and requires risk-management policies for critical infrastructure controlled by artificial intelligence systems. It expressly preserves government action to prevent or abate common-law nuisances from physical datacenter infrastructure. Not a moratorium bill.
field_changes.after: Right to Compute Act. Enrolled section 3 limits government restrictions infringing property/free-expression rights to those demonstrably necessary and narrowly tailored to a compelling government interest. Section 4 requires a reasonable risk-management policy after deploying a critical AI system controlling critical infrastructure; a plan prepared under federal requirements constitutes compliance. Section 7(2)(d) includes prevention or abatement of common-law nuisances created by physical datacenter infrastructure within compelling government interests. This is not a moratorium or blanket exemption from regulation. Later amendments, implementation and current force remain unverified.

Enrolled section 10 provides effect on passage and approval; April 16, 2025 is derived from that clause and the retained official governor-signature event. No sunset is specified in the reviewed enrolled act. Later amendments and present force were not checked.
